armel.role: Current BCM SDK 32-bit ASUS userspace uses armel/softfp; retain this ABI for rebuilt components and links to its vendor objects

armhf.role: Optional compatibility target for additional armhf components installed in the future; not a dependency of the current BCM SDK
armhf.activation: Provide its loader and matching runtime libraries when an additional component requires armhf; do not migrate current SDK components to armhf

arm64.role: Default for new and successfully ported userspace components without incompatible vendor dependencies

not_ubuntu_ready: package.py redirects interpreter to /opt/lib/ld-linux-aarch64.so.1 and embeds USB lib64 plus /opt/lib rpaths
no dpkg ownership, dependencies, triggers, or Ubuntu package split
gcc16_usb_packaging.reuse: Source archive, B53 flags, test programs, and build lessons are reusable; do a fresh distro-layout build rather than copying the staged USB compiler.

glibc_source.adaptation: Preserve glibc 2.44 ldconfig_parse_config callback API while using Ubuntu trusted-dir enumeration; other changes retain Ubuntu logic.

binutils.prior_build_inputs: BE98 older ARM32 cross toolchains use Ubuntu 2.42; newer GCC15 cross trees carry Ubuntu binutils 2.46-3ubuntu2. See actual ld query output for executable versions.
binutils.plan: Rebuild official binutils 2.47 with Ubuntu/Debian packaging, AArch64 host flags -O2 -mcpu=cortex-a53+crypto+crc, and separate aarch64-linux-gnu/arm-linux-gnueabi/arm-linux-gnueabihf targets as needed. Enable and package linker plugin/LTO support, shared dependency metadata, zstd support where packaging provides it. Do not infer speedup from flags; benchmark representative links separately.
binutils.distinction: B53 host CFLAGS tune the tools themselves; target ISA defaults and ABI are separate compiler settings. Never use -march=native on the GB10 build host for router binaries.

ubuntu_layout_contract.vendor_abi: armel softfp (not Ubuntu native armel archive support)
ubuntu_layout_contract.private_vendor_plugins: Retain only audited hardcoded paths as compatibility links or configure/rebuild consumers; BE98 pins cannot be blindly applied to different BE19000AI bytes.
ubuntu_layout_contract.runtime_directories: BE98 /run -> var/run was an ASUS compatibility shim, not a complete Ubuntu model. Essential Ubuntu needs persistent /etc and /var/lib/dpkg,/var/lib/apt with transient /run; do not inherit ASUS whole-/var tmpfs for package state.
ubuntu_layout_contract.package_ownership: Every base/toolchain/runtime/vendor file is owned by a .deb or explicitly documented local configuration; never merely copy a libc/toolchain over dpkg-owned files and leave package metadata stale.
ubuntu_layout_contract.armel_repository: Keep Ubuntu ports entries arch-filtered to supported arm64 and optional armhf. Supply local armel packages from a separately signed project repository; Ubuntu cross packages are SDK payloads, not native armel base packages.

required_rebuilds.recipe: Fresh native arm64 Debian/Ubuntu package build using target aarch64-linux-gnu, prefix /usr, --enable-multiarch, major-version directories and gcc-16/g++-16 entry points. Rebase supported Ubuntu packaging patches onto 16.2.0. Use the real Ubuntu sysroot/header layout and default /lib ABI loader; remove all /opt/USB rpaths. Build separate armel and armhf cross compiler packages if required; AArch64 GCC -m32 does not provide the ARM32 compilers.

required_rebuilds.required: Deb packaging required; existing validated source/patches/stages reusable as reference, not an installed-package substitute.
required_rebuilds.recipe: Rebase current Ubuntu packaging onto pinned release/2.44 source, retaining known multiarch patches and --enable-kernel=4.19. Build coherent libc6/libc-bin/libc6-dev/locales or minimal needed subset and per-ABI libgcc/libstdc++ packages, preserving maintainer scripts/triggers/shlibs/symbols and Multi-Arch semantics. Test dpkg install/upgrade/remove rules in the offline rootfs.
New signed-source build and .deb packaging; no completed B53 2.47 artifact was found in audited checkpoints.

abi_pitfalls: Ubuntu GCC15 ARM32 defaults define _TIME_BITS=64 and _FILE_OFFSET_BITS=64. Earlier BE98 checkpoints cleared them broadly to preserve legacy ABI. Current user policy supersedes that default: new/rebuilt components prefer time64, source bugs are repaired first, and -U is allowed only for a proven individual legacy boundary documented in configs/ubuntu26/layout-profile.json.
armel softfp permits hardware FP/NEON while preserving the soft-float call ABI; do not change vendor calls to hard-float.
Existing kernel9 time64 tests validate the new ARM32 syscall surface, not every syscall required by Ubuntu systemd or every vendor process.
Latest glibc release and kernel minimum are distinct: keep 4.19 fallback assumptions even with backported time64; --enable-kernel=5.1 would assume unrelated newer APIs.

Use one ABI-matched loader/runtime set atomically. Validate cache-disabled and cached resolution, dlopen/plugins, TLS/pthreads, DNS/NSS, crypto and C++ unwinding. Systemd/PID1/vendor service coexistence requires separate QEMU and physical acceptance.
required_acceptance: gcc-16 -dumpmachine=aarch64-linux-gnu and -print-multiarch=aarch64-linux-gnu; both ARM32 compilers report their own tuples.
Compile/link C, C++, DSO, TLS/pthread, exception-unwind and LTO tests for every installed ABI; verify ELF interpreter, symbols, target ISA, actual dependencies and no /opt/USB absolute paths.
dpkg-shlibdeps and apt dependency solver accept package metadata; matching Multi-Arch:same package versions coinstall without conflicting files; package upgrade maintains loader symlinks/cache.
Existing ASUS binaries, private plugins, web UI, Wi-Fi/Runner/AiMesh and the separate AI-board link pass on the final BE19000AI candidate before deployment.
